The idea

Nature’s care.
In your day.

From a personal-care routine to family life and an active day, Natoral has room to grow while keeping one recognisable signature.

Natoral is a nature-first brand spanning body care, haircare, baby foods and supplements, and bodybuilding products. This study presents the supplied packaging family through product compositions, campaign artwork and everyday imagery.

Design
Eyilade Oridamisi
Scope
Identity extension, naming, packaging & art direction
Portfolio development
Product imagery uses the eight label designs supplied for this study. The surrounding scenes are AI-assisted portfolio visualisations with fictional models; product settings and pack sizes remain proposed concepts.

A family, with room to grow

One signature.
Four worlds.

The supplied packaging gives each category its own character through typography, colour, illustration and physical form. Explore all eight designs below.

01 / 04 · Body

Dewskin & Softmelt

Body lotion. Body butter crème.

Pink and burgundy packs pair a fine serif product name with botanical imagery, clear category bands and gold closures. The supplied artwork carries through every scene.

02 / 04 · Hair

Root Ritual & Curl Veil

Shampoo. Leave-in conditioner.

Cobalt and teal, bold white names, yellow category cues and flowing ribbons. The supplied bottle and tube designs bring a fresh, confident voice to haircare.

Supplied packaging family

03 / 04 · Baby

First Spoon & Little Drops

Baby food. Baby supplement.

Warm golden cereal packaging and a separate lavender supplement set. Clear names, category cues and illustrated ingredients distinguish the two supplied designs.

Form Daily

Protein blend. Vanilla & Cocoa.

Black tubs, a white signature band, athletic italic lettering and flavour-led illustration. Vanilla and Cocoa use the supplied labels in every application.

Body · Photography view

The original foundation

A natural gesture.
A distinctive name.

The layered symbol and rounded wordmark are the original work. The source identity keeps its green palette; the supplied category signatures use pink, burgundy, white, purple and black with yellow accents.

A small mark, a wider world

A shape that
holds it together.

The original symbol remains recognisable across every category. Its geometry stays intact while each range develops its own independent graphic language.

The close-up

Care in
the details.

A practical closure. A clear label. A surface that feels tangible. Small decisions give a proposed product a convincing presence.

A familiar name.
A useful object.
A daily ritual.

The supplied Dewskin design comes into focus: pink packaging, a gold pump, a serif product name and carefully layered label information.

In the everyday

For quiet moments.
For busy days.

Natural gestures and contemporary spaces give the brand a human scale.

Baby packaging is shown as supplied. The lifestyle scenes do not depict supplement administration or product consumption.

A voice for the everyday

A little room
for yourself.

Short, direct messages leave the people, the objects and the original signature space to speak.

Beyond the bottle

A thoughtful
arrival.

The supplied body-care products sit alongside a burgundy mailer, fine tissue and a personal note. The experience continues beyond the bottle.

The starting point

The original
work.

The supplied identity established the stacked and horizontal signatures, colour variations and repeat pattern. This study preserves that foundation and builds four distinct category systems around it.

Packaging is reproduced from the supplied N1–N8 artwork. Statements printed on those labels are part of the supplied designs and have not been independently verified. Scenes are portfolio visualisations, not evidence of production or endorsement.
